audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart claimed Lillia wins six of seven stages, contradicting both the packet chart (Skill/Skill/Aatrox/Skill/Skill/Aatrox/Lillia), the 16.67% win rate, and the matchup's own whys text, which says 'it's even' at 1, 'Still even' at 2, 'He spikes hardest here' at 3 and 'His first-item spike' at first item.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row; both said Lillia while the prose under them said even/Aatrox. The mirror (aatrox__lillia.json) left the packet chart in place, so the Aatrox page already reads Aatrox at Level 3 and First item.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped to Skill/Skill/Aatrox/Skill/Skill/Aatrox/Lillia in both layers as one atomic group, with ratings and why lines rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Power spikes were described as Lillia-owned at Level 3 and first item; the real spikes are Aatrox's — his third Darkin Blade angle plus Infernal Chains at 3, and his first-item healing spike.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash both heal, so his first-item power outsustains a Liandry's DoT; Lillia's genuine spike is 2+ items on the open map.
audit.corrected: phases[2].why and phases[5].why now state Aatrox's spikes with his real ability names; phases[6] left as Lillia's reclaim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named a single Aatrox ability except World Ender — the packet flags exactly this defect.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade (14/12/10/8/6s), Infernal Chains (20/18/16/14/12s), Umbral Dash (9/8/7/6/5s) and Deathbringer Stance are what actually decide the lane, and none appeared.
audit.corrected: Real names and cooldowns inserted into the level-chart whys and the enemy-plan lines. NOTE: Infernal Chains carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's description (drag to centre + slow) does not support, so no grounding claim was made — matching the mirror's correction of record.

audit.why: Infernal Chains is his only reliable lock and is down 20s at rank 1 — that is the window to step up.

edits.before: Q's outer ring on his last-hits plus the passive speed means he literally cannot touch you at level 1.
edits.after: Aatrox has one Q charge and no chains, but you have only Q too — chip the outer ring and start the burn.

edits.before: W sweetspot threat starts — anyone chasing you eats the big hit while your Dream Dust burns their HP bar.
edits.after: Still even — W's sweetspot deters a chase, but The Darkin Blade at 14s outranges your step-up trades.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-kite in circles, E from fog for the slow, and the passive speed makes every trade yours to end.
edits.after: His spike: three Darkin Blade angles into Infernal Chains locks you mid-hop and Deathbringer heals off the burn.

edits.before: The lane is a treadmill he can't get off — Q every step-up, kite the World Ender window, and bank Dream Dust burn.
edits.after: Even window — full Q and the burn poke him, but Umbral Dash's heal on every hit refills any trade you extend.

edits.before: Lilting Lullaby online — your jungler's ganks are now guaranteed, and any overstep becomes a sleep-execute.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby lands, but the drowsy delay lets Umbral Dash or World Ender break it — it wins with a jungler.

edits.before: Liandry's spike — Dream Dust plus the burn melts juggernauts and tanks alike while you jog circles around them.
edits.after: His first item plus Deathbringer healing outpaces your Liandry's burn — every extended trade refills him faster.

edits.before: Aatrox's threat window: three Q angles plus W chain-pull means one good knockup into the pull lets his passive heal eat your whole DoT.
edits.after: Aatrox's threat window: three Darkin Blade angles plus Infernal Chains means one knockup into the drag lets Deathbringer Stance eat your whole DoT.

edits.before: Land the third Q knockup into W chain-pull to lock you mid-kite and start his passive healing
edits.after: Land the third Darkin Blade knockup into Infernal Chains, down 20s at rank 1, to lock you and start Deathbringer healing

edits.before: Use E (Swirlseed) to slow him whenever he steps up so his W pull never lands clean
edits.after: Roll Swirlseed (E, 12s flat) into him on every step-up so Infernal Chains never lands clean

notes: Chart proposed in matched full/content pairs as one atomic group. diff ('EVEN'), diffRating 4/10, carryRating 5/10, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t still call this a favoured matchup, which now contradicts the corrected chart and the 16.67% win rate over 12 games — left alone because the mirror made no diff-layer edits and I will not introduce a one-sided rating conflict; flagged for the user. Infernal Chains' derived 'grounding' flag contradicts Riot's description (drag + slow only) and was not used, consistent with the mirror's correction of record. Sample size is only 12 games; the chart change follows the packet chart and the matchup's own prose, not the win rate alone.
